L0@P0: THE CASSELS–TATE PAIRING ON POLARIZED ABELIAN VARIETIES
L1@P0: BJORN POONEN AND MICHAEL STOLL
L2@P0: Abstract. Let (A, λ) be a principally polarized abelian variety defined over a global field
L3@P0: k, and let X(A) be its Shafarevich–Tate group. Let X(A)nd denote the quotient of X(A)
L4@P0: by its maximal divisible subgroup. Cassels and Tate constructed a non-degenerate pairing
L5@P0: X(A)nd × X(A)nd → Q/Z .
L6@P0: If A is an elliptic curve, then by a result of Cassels’ the pairing is alternating. But in general
L7@P0: it is only antisymmetric.
L8@P0: Using some new but equivalent definitions of the pairing, we derive general criteria deciding whether it is alternating and whether there exists some alternating non-degenerate
L9@P0: pairing on X(A)nd. These criteria are expressed in terms of an element c ∈ X(A)nd that is
L10@P0: canonically associated to the polarization λ. In the case that A is the Jacobian of some curve,
L11@P0: a down-to-earth version of the result allows us to determine effectively whether #X(A) (if
L12@P0: finite) is a square or twice a square. We then apply this to prove that a positive proportion
L13@P0: (in some precise sense) of all hyperelliptic curves of even genus g ≥ 2 over Q have a Jacobian
L14@P0: with non-square #X (if finite). For example, it appears that this density is about 13% for
L15@P0: curves of genus 2. The proof makes use of a general result relating global and local densities;
L16@P0: this result can be applied in other situations.

L51@P1: 1. Introduction
L52@P1: The study of the Shafarevich–Tate group X(A) of an abelian variety A over a global field k
L53@P1: is fundamental to the understanding of the arithmetic of A. It plays a role analogous to that
L54@P1: of the class group in the theory of the multiplicative group over an order in k. Cassels [Ca],
L55@P1: in one of the first papers devoted to the study of X, proved that in the case where E is an
L56@P1: elliptic curve over a number field, there exists a pairing
L57@P1: X(E) × X(E) −→ Q/Z
L58@P1: that becomes nondegenerate after one divides X(E) by its maximal divisible subgroup. He
L59@P1: proved also that this pairing is alternating; i.e., that hx, xi = 0 for all x. If, as is conjectured,
L60@P1: X(E) is always finite, then this would force its order to be a perfect square. Tate [Ta2]
L61@P1: soon generalized Cassels’ results by proving that for abelian varieties A and their duals A∨
L62@P1: in general, there is a pairing
L63@P1: X(A) × X(A
L64@P1: ∨
L65@P1: ) −→ Q/Z,
L66@P1: that is nondegenerate after dividing by maximal divisible subgroups. He also proved that if
L67@P1: X(A) is mapped to X(A∨) via a polarization arising from a k-rational divisor on A then
L68@P1: the induced pairing on X(A) is alternating. But it is known that when dim A > 1, a krational polarization need not come from a k-rational divisor on A. (See Section 4 for the
L69@P1: obstruction.) For principally polarized abelian varieties in general1, Flach [Fl] proved that
L70@P1: the pairing is antisymmetric, by which we mean hx, yi = −hy, xi for all x, y, which is slightly
